newsitem.title: USA: Plane crashes on golf course: misses O.J. Simpson.
newsitem.headline: Plane crashes on golf course: misses O.J. Simpson.

text.p: A light plane crashed on a golf course on Friday evening, just a few hundred yards (metres) from where O.J. Simpson was playing while a jury deliberated in his civil trial, officials said.
The single-engine aircraft, which had radioed it had a mechanical problem, came down on the second fairway of the Rancho Park course in suburban Cheviot Hills, where Simpson regularly plays.
The pilot and a passenger were injured and one of the men was transported to a nearby hospital.

Ralph Hoag, a golfer who helped pull the two men from the badly damaged plane, said that after rescuing the pair, a player came over from the next fairway and said, "do you know O.J. Simpson is over there?"

The course manager, Robert Cosarez, later confirmed to reporters that the ex-football star had been playing when the plane came down. There was no comment from Simpson, who packed up and left the course soon after the crash, witnesses said.

Ironically, during closing arguments in the punitive damages phase of Simpson's wrongful death civil trial in Santa Monica on Friday, plaintiffs' attorney Daniel Petrocelli pointed out to the jury that Simpson was absent.
Petrocelli told the panel to send Simpson a message "to whatever golf course he is on" by ordering him to pay a large amount of punitive damages.

On Tuesday, the same jury found Simpson responsible for the deaths of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, and ordered him to pay $8.5 million in compensatory damages. The jury resumes deliberations on punitive damages on Monday.
